title: When They Demand a Supermarket Snack | Parenting Rewind
description:
Your five-year-old spots a snack and treats no like an emergency. A practical pause-and-rewind response for parents.

General parenting education; every child and family is different.
audience_intent: Adults and parents; not directed to children
education_scope: General parenting education only; not personalised therapy, diagnosis, or medical advice.

narration.transcript: Your five-year-old spots a snack and treats no like an emergency. A rushed no, followed by a lecture about sugar, adds attention without making the limit clearer. Before reacting, pause for one breath so the next words can be short, clear, and useful. Pause, get close, and say: We are not buying that today; you may choose apples or bananas for the trolley. Acknowledge disappointment, offer only choices you can accept, and keep shopping without reopening the decision.

source.organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
source.title: Steps for Giving Good Directions

claim_limits: The suggested wording is an example, not a guarantee.
Families should adapt expectations to age, development, safety and individual needs.
